items.author: Randi Kaye
items.excerpt: In September this year, I found myself standing atop a mountain outside Park City, Utah, nearly 10,000 feet above sea level, crying like I haven’t cried in years. Why I was there is complicated. So is what I learned from it. But there I was, at age 58, outfitted with a hydration vest, a headlamp, and enough snacks and electrolytes to keep me alive for weeks. I was chasing something. Freedom? Power? Strength? Adventure? Maybe all of that, but I was also looking to let go of something — to leave something behind that I’d been carrying for decades.
